events.title: The Second Shape
events.summary: Your work is stable, but stability is not the same as meaning.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A former colleague offers you a role on a difficult project in a new city. The salary is only slightly better. The learning curve is not.

choices.label: Take the leap and move for the project.
Negotiate time, pay and a clear exit plan.
Stay. Your life here has value too.

jump.speaker: narrator
jump.text: The first month is messy. By the third, you know exactly which kind of difficult work makes you feel more alive.

negotiate.speaker: narrator
negotiate.text: The revised offer is not perfect, but it respects the shape of the life you are already building.

stay.speaker: narrator
stay.text: You turn down a story other people would have admired. The ordinary life you keep becomes more intentional.

events.title: The Call at 6:10
events.summary: Care becomes a practical decision, not an abstract virtue.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A family member needs help coordinating appointments and paperwork. Everyone cares. Nobody has a plan.

choices.label: Build a schedule and share the work across the family.
Pay for a service and protect everyone's time.

share.speaker: narrator
share.text: The work is still tiring, but no one becomes invisible inside it. A family calendar turns out to be a form of love.

pay.speaker: narrator
pay.text: Money does not solve the hard parts. It does buy breathing room, which is sometimes the hard part you needed.

burnout.speaker: narrator
burnout.text: You become the person who knows every detail and has no energy left to speak. Eventually, the family notices.

events.title: What the Money Is For
events.summary: A financial milestone asks what you want it to change.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Your accounts are finally comfortable. A younger person asks how you made it, expecting a trick. You remember the years when every decision had a face.

choices.label: Mentor someone and make the path less lonely.
Fund a practical scholarship or community project.
Keep building security for your household.

mentor.speaker: narrator
mentor.text: The advice is less glamorous than the question wanted: keep records, ask for help, and do not confuse speed with progress.

give.speaker: narrator
give.text: The project is small enough to understand and useful enough to outlive the photo from its launch day.

keep.speaker: narrator
keep.text: Security is not selfish when it gives the people you love room to breathe. You keep your promises quietly.

events.title: The Empty Desk
events.summary: The future arrives as a room you are no longer required to fill.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Your calendar has more empty space than it has in decades. The first morning feels like freedom. The second feels like a question.

choices.label: Start one last creative project with no growth target.
Make time the main thing and be present with family.
Teach the skills you once had to learn alone.

create.speaker: narrator
create.text: Without a market to impress, the work becomes honest. You finish it because finishing feels good.

family.speaker: narrator
family.text: The photographs are ordinary. That is why you keep them.

teach.speaker: narrator
teach.text: A student asks a question you once thought was obvious. You remember how much kindness lives inside a good explanation.

conclusions.title: Open Horizon
conclusions.text: The first adult choices have become a pattern: work, love, money, health, and the occasional surprise that changes the route. The horizon opens.

conclusions.title: A Second Shape
conclusions.text: You stop treating your first plan as a contract. A life can keep its values while changing its shape.

conclusions.title: The Care Year
conclusions.text: You learn that responsibility is not a single brave act. It is a system built so nobody has to be brave every day.

conclusions.title: Enough to Share
conclusions.text: The numbers matter. So do the people the numbers made possible.

conclusions.title: The Long View
conclusions.text: A life is not measured only by what it accumulates. It is also the questions it makes easier for someone else to ask.
